workers.title: Worker registration keys
workers.description: Create one-time registration tokens for Hermes, OpenClaw, ZeroClaw, and similar workers. Pin a provider when a worker must use a specific {{tenantName}} LLM backend.
workers.quickAccessDescription: Open the Workers tab to create registration keys, set permissions, choose a provider, and apply quotas.
workers.createDescription: Generate a short-lived worker bootstrap key. Keep the raw token secret and copy it only once.
workers.label: Key label
workers.expiryHint: Leave blank for a non-expiring key, or set a short lifespan for safer bootstrap.
workers.invalidExpiry: Enter a valid expiry day number, or leave it blank for no expiry.
workers.providerRequired: Pick a provider before creating a pinned worker key.
workers.copyNow: Copy this token now. It will not be shown again after you leave this screen.
workers.listDescription: Manage issued keys and revoke any token you no longer trust.
workers.guidanceBody: Create a key here, copy the token once, and paste it into the Hermes/OpenClaw worker bootstrap configuration. The selected provider pin travels with the token so {{tenantName}} can route the gateway deterministically.
workers.invalidQuota: Enter valid quota numbers, or leave the fields blank for unlimited usage.
workers.quotas.title: Credit quotas
workers.quotas.summary: Set optional credit caps for this worker key. Leave any field blank to make it unlimited.
workers.quotas.hint: These values map to the worker budget policy after registration. Empty means no cap.
workers.quotas.tip1: Use a short-lived key for the first connection test, then extend the quota only after the worker is trusted.
workers.quotas.tip2: If the worker should never exceed a fixed budget, set the smallest hourly or daily cap that still lets it finish its job.
workers.quotas.tip3: Leave quota fields blank when you want the owner's normal tenant budget rules to apply instead.
workers.permissions.title: Permissions
workers.permissions.description: Pick a preset or switch to Custom to fine-tune scopes one by one.
workers.permissions.scopesHint: Click checkboxes to allow the worker to use specific gateway families and workspace features.
workers.permissions.summary: Permissions travel with the key and help {{tenantName}} decide what the worker may request after registration.
workers.permissions.tip1: Read-only keys are best for simple assistants and first-time setup.
workers.permissions.tip2: Use a pinned provider only when you need a specific backend for compatibility or policy reasons.
workers.permissions.tip3: Custom scopes should be the minimum set the worker actually needs.
workers.permissions.groups.gateway.title: Gateway and LLM
workers.permissions.groups.gateway.descr: Model calls, delegated HTTP, delegated MCP, and callbacks.
workers.permissions.groups.knowledge.des: Files, library access, and RAG read/write operations.
Allow the worker to execute skills or agent workflows.
workers.permissions.groups.workOs.title: Work OS
workers.permissions.groups.workOs.descri: Read or write work items and operating queues.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.r: Best for safe first-time registration with minimal access.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.o: Adds delegation and publish rights for normal operations.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.c: Good for content generation and media-heavy workflows.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.k: Optimized for library, RAG, and knowledge-centric work.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.w: Focused on work intake, queues, and operating tasks.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.f: All supported scopes for a power-user worker.
workers.permissions.presetDescriptions.c: Manually choose only the scopes you want.
workers.guide.step1: Choose the worker type, then decide whether the LLM should auto-select a provider or stay pinned to one provider.
workers.guide.step2: Pick a permission preset, then refine the allowed scopes if the preset is not exact enough.
workers.guide.step3: Set hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly credit caps only when you want to limit usage; leave any field blank for unlimited.
workers.guide.step4: Create the key, copy the token once, and paste it into the Hermes/OpenClaw bootstrap flow.
workers.guide.step5: Revoke the key any time if the token is leaked, no longer needed, or should not be used again.
workers.safety.title: Safety checklist
workers.safety.tip1: Use short expiries for temporary setup keys.
workers.safety.tip2: Prefer the smallest permission set that still lets the worker do the job.
workers.safety.tip3: Pin a provider only when deterministic routing matters.
workers.safety.tip4: Revoke unused keys regularly and review the audit trail after registration.
workers.connect.title: How to connect the worker
workers.connect.description: After you create the key, open the worker's own bootstrap or registration screen, paste the token into its registration field, and start the worker once.
workers.connect.hermes.title: Hermes
workers.connect.hermes.description: Use Hermes when the bridge is managed by the Hermes runtime and you want {{tenantName}} to own policy and credits.
workers.connect.hermes.step1: Open the Hermes container or bridge setup and choose the registration/bootstrap flow.
workers.connect.hermes.step2: Paste the worker access token into the registration token field and keep the provider pin if you selected one.
workers.connect.hermes.step3: Finish setup, then check Admin Monitoring to confirm the worker registered successfully.
workers.connect.openclaw.title: OpenClaw
workers.connect.openclaw.description: Use OpenClaw when the worker already knows how to register with the {{tenantName}} control plane.
workers.connect.openclaw.step1: Open the OpenClaw worker bootstrap or enrollment screen.
workers.connect.openclaw.step2: Paste the token into the worker registration key or bootstrap token field.
workers.connect.openclaw.step3: Start the worker, then bind it to a team if you want it to receive team work.
workers.connect.zeroclaw.title: ZeroClaw
workers.connect.zeroclaw.description: Use ZeroClaw for desktop-managed workers that connect from a device you control.
workers.connect.zeroclaw.step1: Open the ZeroClaw desktop or device enrollment flow.
workers.connect.zeroclaw.step2: Paste the token into the registration key field and save the device identity if prompted.
workers.connect.zeroclaw.step3: Complete enrollment and verify the worker appears online in monitoring.
workers.connect.nemoclaw.title: NemoClaw
workers.connect.nemoclaw.description: Use NemoClaw for sandboxed workers that register into a secure pool.
workers.connect.nemoclaw.step1: Open the NemoClaw sandbox registration or pool bootstrap screen.
workers.connect.nemoclaw.step2: Paste the token into the sandbox registration field before the first start.
workers.connect.nemoclaw.step3: Launch the sandbox and confirm the worker enters the expected pool in monitoring.
